api.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: XRG completed a second acquisition from a GIP vehicle, taking a 7.6% aggregate interest across Trains 4 and 5 while GIP retained a residual stake.
NextDecade reported Trains 1 and 2 at 74.0% completion, Train 3 at 50.4%, Train 4 at 15.5% and Train 5 at 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027.
The Train 5 equity transaction closed with NextDecade at 50%, GIP at 36.9% and GIC/Mubadala holding a combined 13.2% at entry.
XRG completed its acquisition of an 11.7% indirect Phase 1 interest from a GIP vehicle, reducing but not eliminating GIP's ownership.
The Train 4 equity transaction closed with NextDecade at 40%, GIP at 36.9%, TotalEnergies at 10%, GIC at 7.9% and Mubadala at 5.2% at entry.
Rio Grande LNG reached Phase 1 final investment decision and closed the joint-venture equity transaction with GIP, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

api.subsector: Electric utilities and global power generation
api.description: The AES Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-headquartered power and utilities company with regulated utilities, conventional generation, renewable energy, battery storage and related infrastructure across the United States and international markets. Its customers include regulated residential, commercial and industrial utility users, corporate and technology buyers, utilities and wholesale-market counterparties. AES remained publicly owned as of August 23, 2026. A consortium jointly controlled by GIP-managed vehicles and EQT Infrastructure VI signed an agreement on March 1, 2026 to acquire 100% of AES through Horizon Parent, L.P.; CalPERS and QIA are also participants. Stockholders approved the merger and the HSR waiting period expired in June 2026, but other regulatory reviews remained open and no legal closing was found. GIP, EQT, CalPERS and QIA are therefore pending buyers, not current owners.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

The AES Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-headquartered power and utilities company with regulated utilities, conventional generation, renewable energy, battery storage and related infrastructure across the United States and international markets.

Its customers include regulated residential, commercial and industrial utility users, corporate and technology buyers, utilities and wholesale-market counterparties. AES remained publicly owned as of August 23, 2026. A consortium jointly controlled by GIP-managed vehicles and EQT Infrastructure VI signed an agreement on March 1, 2026 to acquire 100% of AES through Horizon Parent, L.P.; CalPERS and QIA are also participants. Stockholders approved the merger and the HSR waiting period expired in June 2026, but other regulatory reviews remained open and no legal closing was found. GIP, EQT, CalPERS and QIA are therefore pending buyers, not current owners.

STORY TIMELINE
Jun 26, 2026

AES stockholders approved the merger after the HSR waiting period expired; other regulatory approvals and legal closing remained pending.

Mar 2, 2026
Acquisition

AES announced a definitive agreement for a GIP- and EQT-led consortium to acquire 100% of the company through Horizon Parent, L.P.

Applied Energy Services, Inc., now The AES Corporation, was incorporated.
